steps.title: The rule: Validated environment-based configuration with fail-fast startup

blocks.text: Subclass BaseSettings from pydantic_settings and declare typed fields to load and validate external configuration.

Construct Settings() to read environment variables and validate their types, with missing required settings or invalid values producing validation failures. Use SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env") as model_config when a dotenv file should provide settings; environment variables take precedence over its values.

segments.label: Declare typed settings and replace a default through the environment
segments.summary: A configuration module defines Settings by importing BaseSettings from pydantic_settings and subclassing it. The class declares app_name as a string with a default. Constructing Settings creates an object whose fields can be accessed by the application. The example first uses the default name, then supplies APP_NAME in the environment for a command. The resulting settings object uses that environment value instead of the default.

bridge.before: Watch how the typed app_name declaration becomes a constructed settings object. The clip uses a default; the text also teaches required settings without defaults.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates environment loading, but not missing-required or invalid-value failures, dotenv configuration, or dotenv precedence. The text covers those rules so configuration can be validated before serving.
